The answer is E.

promptHTML: A data set has standard deviation 15. Every value x is replaced by (35 − 3x)/5. What is the standard deviation of the new data set?
explanation: SD ignores shifts and sign, and scales by |coefficient|: new SD = |−3/5| × 15 = 9. The “35” and the minus sign are decoys — adding a constant never changes SD, and reflecting the data flips signs of deviations but not their squares.

promptHTML: A list of 15 observations has (population) variance 48. A 16th observation, exactly equal to the mean of the original 15, is appended. What is the variance of the 16 observations?
explanation: The new value sits on the mean, so the mean is unchanged and it contributes zero squared deviation. Sum of squared deviations stays 15 × 48 = 720, now divided by 16: variance = 720/16 = 45. Rule: appending a value equal to the mean always shrinks variance by the factor n/(n+1).

promptHTML: Group P has 20 observations with mean 30 and standard deviation 5. Group Q has 30 observations with mean 40 and standard deviation 10. What is the variance of the combined group of 50 observations?
explanation: Combined mean = (20·30 + 30·40)/50 = 36. Combined variance = weighted mean of (variance + squared distance of group mean from combined mean): [20(25 + 36) + 30(100 + 16)]/50 = (1220 + 3480)/50 = 94. Averaging the two variances (62.5) ignores the between-group spread — the classic error.

promptHTML: Seven positive integers (not necessarily distinct) have mean 20 and median 25. What is the greatest possible value of the largest integer?
explanation: Sum = 140, and the 4th value in sorted order is 25, forcing the 5th and 6th to be at least 25. To maximise the largest, minimise everything else: 1, 1, 1, 25, 25, 25 leaves 140 − 78 = 62. Forgetting that the two values above the median must also be ≥ 25 gives the trap answer 68.

promptHTML: Nine distinct positive integers have mean 30. What is the greatest possible value of the median?
explanation: Sum = 270. Median is the 5th of 9 sorted values. Minimise the bottom four as 1, 2, 3, 4 (sum 10). If the median is m, distinctness forces the top five to total at least m + (m+1) + (m+2) + (m+3) + (m+4) = 5m + 10. So 5m + 20 ≤ 270 ⇒ m ≤ 50, achieved by {1,2,3,4,50,51,52,53,54}. Answer: 50.

promptHTML: A list of 10 positive integers has a unique mode of 7 occurring exactly 4 times, median 9, and mean 12. What is the greatest possible value of the largest element?
explanation: Sum = 120; the four 7s are the smallest values (28), so the 5th and 6th values must average 9. Take them as 9, 9. To free up budget, make the 7th–9th values as small as possible without creating a rival mode: 9 can appear once more (three 9s < four 7s), then 10, 10. That uses 28 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 10 + 10 = 75, leaving 45. Any attempt with 8, 10 as the middle pair wastes more (checking: max 43). Constructed list: {7,7,7,7,9,9,9,10,10,45}.

promptHTML:
A data set D of 25 values has mean μ and standard deviation σ > 0. Which of the following operations leave the standard deviation exactly unchanged?

I. Appending the two values μ + σ and μ − σ
II. Appending the value μ twice
III. Multiplying every value by −1
explanation: I: the mean stays μ (the two new values are symmetric), and they add exactly σ² + σ² to the squared-deviation total: new variance = (25σ² + 2σ²)/27 = σ² — unchanged. II: adds zero spread but increases n, so SD shrinks. III: every deviation flips sign but squares identically — unchanged. Answer: I and III.

promptHTML: 200 students took a test. The mean score is 62 and the standard deviation is 8. No assumption is made about the shape of the distribution. At least how many students must have scored strictly between 46 and 78?
explanation: 46 and 78 are exactly 2 standard deviations from the mean. By Chebyshev’s inequality, at most 1/k² = 1/4 of any distribution lies k = 2 or more SDs from the mean, so at least 3/4 of 200 = 150 lie strictly inside. 190 (the 95% empirical rule) is the trap — that requires a normal distribution, which is not given.

promptHTML: Ten numbers have Σx = 60 and Σx² = 1000. Each number is increased by 5. What is the sum of the squares of the new numbers?
explanation: Σ(x+5)² = Σx² + 10Σx + 25n = 1000 + 600 + 250 = 1850. Dropping the cross term 2·5·Σx gives the trap 1250. (Bonus check: the SD is √(1000/10 − 6²) = 8 before and after the shift.)

promptHTML: A school has sections A, B and C with average scores 62, 74 and 85. Section C has twice as many students as section A, the three sections total 60 students, and the overall average is exactly 75. How many students are in section B?
explanation: Let A have a students, so C has 2a and B has 60 − 3a. Total score: 62a + 74(60 − 3a) + 170a = 4500 ⇒ 10a + 4440 = 4500 ⇒ a = 6. So B = 60 − 18 = 42. Check: (372 + 3108 + 1020)/60 = 75. ✓

promptHTML: M is the combined multiset (duplicates kept) of all multiples of 3 from 3 to 60 and all multiples of 4 from 4 to 80 — 40 numbers in total. What is the median of M?
explanation: The median is the average of the 20th and 21st smallest. Count of elements ≤ t is ⌊t/3⌋ + ⌊t/4⌋ (common multiples like 12, 24, 36 are counted twice — it is a multiset). At t = 35 the count is 11 + 8 = 19; at t = 36 it jumps by two (36 is both a multiple of 3 and of 4) to 21. So the 20th and 21st values are both 36: median = 36.

promptHTML: Six numbers have mean 50 and range exactly 20. What is the maximum possible standard deviation?
explanation: With range 20 the values live in an interval [m, m+20]. Spread is maximised by pushing values to the endpoints; keeping the mean at 50 forces the endpoints to be symmetric: 40 and 60, three values each. Variance = 10² = 100, SD = 10. Any asymmetric split (e.g. endpoints 45/65) puts unequal weights on the endpoints and yields less. SD can never exceed half the range.

promptHTML: Scores 1–5 have frequencies: score 1 → 3, score 2 → 5, score 3 → x, score 4 → 7, score 5 → 5, where x is a positive integer. What is the smallest x for which the median score is exactly 3?
explanation: n = 20 + x. Cumulative counts: ≤2 is 8, ≤3 is 8 + x. The median position(s) must fall inside the block of 3s. For x = 4 (n = 24) the 12th value is 3 but the 13th is 4 → median 3.5. For x = 5 (n = 25) the 13th value is the last 3 → median exactly 3. Answer: 5.

promptHTML: 25 test scores have mean 48. The five lowest scores average 20 and the five highest average 70. What is the mean of the remaining 15 scores?
explanation: Total = 25 × 48 = 1200. Remove the tails: 1200 − 5·20 − 5·70 = 1200 − 100 − 350 = 750, over 15 scores = 50. Note the middle mean exceeds the overall mean because the low tail is more extreme than the high tail.

promptHTML: Class A has mean score 70 and class B has mean score 82; together their mean is 79. The total number of students is less than 100, and B has more than 40 students more than A. How many values are possible for the total number of students?
explanation: Alligation: A : B = (82 − 79) : (79 − 70) = 1 : 3, so A = k, B = 3k. Conditions: 4k < 100 and 3k − k = 2k > 40 ⇒ 20 < k < 25 ⇒ k ∈ {21, 22, 23, 24} — 4 possible totals (84, 88, 92, 96).

promptHTML: Two numbers are drawn at random, without replacement, from the set {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}. What is the expected value of the positive difference between them?
explanation: All C(5,2) = 10 pairs are equally likely. The differences are 2,4,6,8 (with 1), 2,4,6 (with 3), 2,4 (with 5), 2 (with 7) — total 40. E = 40/10 = 4. Symmetric shortcut: for equally spaced values with gap d, E|X−Y| = d(n+1)/3 = 2·6/3 = 4.

promptHTML: Five positive integers (not necessarily distinct) have mean 30 and median 30. What is the greatest possible value of the range?
explanation: Sorted a₁ ≤ a₂ ≤ 30 ≤ a₄ ≤ a₅ with sum 150. Maximise a₅ and minimise a₁: set a₁ = a₂ = 1 and a₄ = 30 (it cannot go below the median): a₅ = 150 − 1 − 1 − 30 − 30 = 88. Range = 88 − 1 = 87. Letting a₄ drop below 30 is the standard error (gives 90).

promptHTML: How many quadruples (a, b, c, d) of positive integers with a ≤ b ≤ c ≤ d have mean 5 and median 5?
explanation: Sum = 20 and b + c = 10, so a + d = 10 as well. The ordering needs a ≤ b ≤ c ≤ d; since c = 10 − b and d = 10 − a, the condition c ≤ d is automatic when a ≤ b. So for each b from 1 to 5 (b ≤ c forces b ≤ 5), a ranges over 1..b: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15.

promptHTML: A set S of numbers has standard deviation 12. A new set T contains, for every x in S, both x and x + 10. What is the standard deviation of T?
explanation: T is S overlaid with a copy of itself shifted by 10. The new mean sits 5 above S’s mean; each element of the original copy deviates (x − μ) − 5 and each shifted element (x − μ) + 5. Squaring and averaging: Var(T) = σ² + 25 = 144 + 25 = 169 ⇒ SD = 13. General rule: duplicating with shift c adds (c/2)² to the variance; adding c² = 100 (→ √244 ≈ 15.62) is the trap.

promptHTML: From the integers 1 to 100, every multiple of 7 is deleted. What is the median of the 86 remaining numbers?
explanation: 14 multiples of 7 are removed. The median is the average of the 43rd and 44th survivors. Survivors ≤ t number t − ⌊t/7⌋: at t = 50 that is 50 − 7 = 43, so the 43rd survivor is 50; 51 is not a multiple of 7, so the 44th is 51. Median = 50.5.
